title: Lassonde-backed Cadillac drilling points to more Ontario gold
mineex_summary: Cadillac Mines reported new infill drill results at its Kerr-Addison property in Ontario, including hole KAD26-428T which cut about 23 metres grading 3.08 grams gold per tonne, and hole KAD26-397 which returned 2.13 grams gold over 38 metres. The company said the results demonstrate continuity within the open-pit shell and intersect mineralization beyond current resource limits, according to a Desjardins Securities analyst, ahead of a planned preliminary economic assessment targeted for the third quarter of next year.
plain_english_explanation:
• g/t (grams per tonne): a measure of gold grade in the rock, indicating how much gold is contained per tonne of material.
• Infill drilling: drilling between existing widely spaced holes to better define and increase confidence in a known mineralized zone.
• Step-out drilling: drilling outside the currently defined resource area to test for potential extensions of mineralization.
• Preliminary economic assessment (PEA): an early-stage study estimating the potential economics of a project; it does not confirm a mine will be built.
• Indicated resource: a resource category with a reasonable level of confidence, but still an estimate, not proven reserves ready for mining.
Note: intercept grades reported here reflect drill results and support potential resource conversion or expansion, but do not by themselves establish that a larger resource has been defined or that the project is economic.
context: Cadillac is almost two-thirds through a planned 17,850-metre infill drilling program within the Kerr-Addison open-pit resource; the release covers assays from the first 29 infill holes. The company is targeting lesser-drilled footwall zones within the pit that had historically received less attention than the main break, and plans a step-out program to the northeast of known resource blocks. The current infill program is planned for completion by mid-September, with a preliminary economic assessment targeted for the third quarter of next year.

title: Omai values Guyana gold project at $4B
mineex_summary: Omai Gold Mines released a new preliminary economic assessment (PEA) for its namesake project in Guyana, showing a $4-billion after-tax net present value at a 5% discount rate and a $3,600 per oz. gold price assumption, against $1.42 billion in initial capital costs. The PEA outlines a 24% internal rate of return, a 4.1-year payback period, and projects mining 6.3 million oz. of gold over an 18-year mine life. This updated study follows an April 2024 PEA that covered only the Wenot open pit and about 1.84 million oz. of resources, with a lower NPV of $556 million at a $1,950 per oz. gold price.
plain_english_explanation:
• PEA (Preliminary Economic Assessment): an early-stage economic study estimating whether a project could be profitable to develop; it is not a final feasibility study and carries more uncertainty.
• NPV (Net Present Value): the estimated value today of future project cash flows, discounted at a stated rate (here 5%) — a common way to compare project economics, sensitive to the gold price assumption used.
• IRR (Internal Rate of Return): the estimated annual percentage return the project could generate on invested capital.
• Payback period: the estimated time needed for project cash flow to repay the initial capital investment.
• Indicated and inferred resources: categories describing confidence levels in estimated mineral quantities — indicated resources are estimated with a reasonable level of confidence, while inferred resources have a lower level of geological confidence and are not yet proven to be economically mineable.
• g/t (grams per tonne): a measure of ore grade, showing how much gold is contained per tonne of rock.
context: The new PEA comes four months after Omai released a resource update showing it hosts one of the largest gold resources in Guyana. It updates and expands on an April 2024 PEA that covered only the Wenot open pit and roughly 1.84 million oz. of resources; the new PEA reflects the full project including the open-pit Wenot deposit and the adjacent underground Gilt deposit. Drilling is ongoing at Wenot with five rigs, which Omai's CEO said opens the possibility of further growth at the site.

title: Friedland’s forgotten metal wins $400M US backing
mineex_summary: Sunrise Energy Metals secured a $400-million conditional loan commitment from the US Department of Defense for its Syerston scandium project in New South Wales, Australia, and is also pursuing a US securities exchange listing. The company's updated capital expenditure estimate has risen to A$450-475 million, nearly four times a March feasibility study estimate, reflecting consideration of a US processing plant and a plan to triple planned output to 180 tonnes.
plain_english_explanation:
• Conditional loan commitment: a financing pledge from the US Department of Defense that depends on certain conditions being met before funds are released.
• Measured and indicated / inferred resources: categories reflecting differing levels of geological confidence — measured and indicated resources are more confidently defined than inferred resources, and neither category by itself confirms an economically mineable deposit.
• ppm (parts per million): a unit for measuring low-concentration grades, here used for scandium content in the deposit.
• Feasibility study: a technical/economic study assessing whether a project can be built and operated profitably; changes to cost estimates since the prior study are noted in the source.
• Final investment decision (FID): the point at which a company formally commits to build a project; Sunrise says it plans to reach this by year-end.
context: Sunrise Energy Metals CEO Sam Riggall said the project was originally advanced for its nickel-cobalt resource before pivoting to scandium after Indonesian nickel supply increases; the DoD financing also provides a right of first offer on Sunrise's output. The company plans a final investment decision by year-end, with early works already under way and potential production beginning in 2028. The source also notes a July 8 report from Hunterbrook Capital raising doubts about fuel-cell company Bloom Energy's scandium supply chain, which Bloom disputed.

title: Empire Metals shares jump as Pitfield titanium resource hits 8.2B tonnes
mineex_summary: Empire Metals announced an upgraded mineral resource estimate for its Pitfield titanium project in Western Australia, now totaling 8.16 billion tonnes grading 4.3% titanium dioxide across the Thomas and Cosgrove deposits, which the company says makes it the world's largest titanium resource. The update includes Pitfield's first measured resource category, and shares rose more than 13% on the news. The company states the resource remains at the development stage, with economic studies still needed to determine commercial viability.
plain_english_explanation:
• Mineral resource estimate (MRE): a technical calculation of the quantity and grade of mineralization in a deposit, based on geological data — it is not the same as an economically mineable reserve.
• Measured/Indicated/Inferred: categories reflecting increasing geological confidence, with measured being the most confident and inferred the least; inferred resources have the lowest level of confidence and cannot be used in economic studies without further work.
• Titanium dioxide (TiO2) grade: the percentage of the rock that is titanium dioxide, used in pigments, metal feedstock, and industrial applications.
• Flowsheet: a designed sequence of processing steps used to extract and purify a mineral from ore; here used to describe production of 99% pure titanium dioxide via conventional methods.
• The article notes that resource size and grade do not by themselves establish that a project can be mined economically — further studies are needed.
context: The upgrade establishes Pitfield's first measured resource category, which the company says increases confidence in the deposit's scale and geological continuity as it advances mine planning and economic studies. The update follows a recently demonstrated integrated flowsheet producing 99% pure titanium dioxide using conventional processing steps. The company's next step is to determine whether the resource can support an economically viable operation using this processing route, with the project also having existing rail connections to ports serving Asia, the US, Europe and Saudi Arabia.
